final_candidates.decision_summary: C61 is a validated cancer-associated missense variant in the BRCA1 RING domain that disrupts the BRCA1-BARD1 E3 ubiquitin ligase interface. Tyr substitution preserves the hydrophobic/structural character sufficiently that overall folding is largely retained.
C64 is a zinc-coordinating RING cysteine; C64Y is a documented pathogenic variant abolishing E3 ligase and tumor-suppressor activity. Domain expression is retained despite the loss of a Zn ligand.
C24 coordinates Zn in the RING domain and is structurally essential for the BARD1 interaction. C24Y is expected to abolish ligase function with a modestly higher folding risk than C61Y/C64Y.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates are stable and well-justified; additional self-iteration without external evidence would not improve them.

history.rationale: Cys61 is a core zinc-coordinating residue of the RING domain; substitution with a bulky aromatic residue disrupts the Zn2+-binding fold, abolishing BARD1 heterodimerization and E3 ubiquitin ligase tumor-suppressor activity while leaving the rest of the 1863-aa protein largely intact.

C61 is a validated cancer-associated missense variant in the BRCA1 RING domain that disrupts the BRCA1-BARD1 E3 ubiquitin ligase interface; Tyr substitution is well tolerated structurally, so folding is largely preserved.

Cys64 is the second RING-domain zinc-ligating cysteine; replacing it with tyrosine destroys metal coordination and the RING fold, eliminating BRCA1's E3 ligase function without extensive unfolding of the full-length protein.
C64 is a zinc-coordinating RING cysteine; C64Y is a documented pathogenic variant abolishing ligase/tumor-suppressor activity while retaining substantial domain expression.
Cys24 is the first zinc-chelating cysteine of the RING domain; a Tyr substitution breaks the IIA zinc site, functionally inactivating the N-terminal tumor-suppressor module.
C24 is also a Zn-coordinating RING cysteine; validated in structural studies as essential for BARD1 interaction. Slightly higher structural risk than C61/C64, so confidence held below the top two.

Lys1702 is a conserved BRCT-domain residue critical for phospho-peptide (ABRAXAS/PALB2) binding; charge reversal to Glu disrupts the phosphoserine-binding pocket, abrogating DNA-damage recruitment while keeping the fold largely intact.
K1702 sits in the BRCT repeat; charge-reversal there is a known deleterious class, but BRCT loss is a more indirect route to tumor-suppressor loss than RING zinc disruption.
Arg1699 is a well-characterized pathogenic BRCT missense site; the bulky Trp perturbs the BRCT hydrophobic core and abolishes phosphoprotein interactions with modest structural compromise.
R1699 is within BRCT repeat 1; Trp substitution is a common pathogenic-missense pattern but functional evidence is weaker than for the RING cysteines.
Ser1655 sits in the BRCT repeat interface; Pro introduction locally destabilizes the tandem BRCT scaffold needed for BACH1/ABRAXAS binding, impairing homologous recombination repair.
S1655 is not in a well-characterized functional core; Pro introduction may locally destabilize the BRCT linker without a strong functional-ablation rationale.

rejection.reason: S1655 is not in a well-characterized functional core; Pro introduction may locally destabilize the BRCT linker without a strong functional-ablation rationale.

history.rationale: Cys39 chelates zinc in the RING IIB site; Tyr substitution eliminates metal binding, inactivating the E3 ligase tumor-suppressor function.
C39 is another RING-domain zinc ligand; substitution impairs E3 ligase function but may destabilize the fold more than C61/C64 variants.
Cys44 is a RING-domain zinc ligand whose replacement disrupts the Zn2+ site and BARD1 dimerization, with functional loss comparable to other RING cysteine mutants.
C44 contributes to the second zinc coordination site; disruption is functional but redundant with higher-confidence C61/C64.
Thr1691 is a critical BRCT repeat-interface residue (equivalent to the t1691 stability determinant); alanine substitution weakens the BRCT fold and phosphoprotein binding.
T1691 is peripheral to the BRCT phospho-peptide binding pocket; Ala substitution is unlikely to fully abolish tumor-suppressor function.

rejection.reason: T1691 is peripheral to the BRCT phospho-peptide binding pocket; Ala substitution is unlikely to fully abolish tumor-suppressor function.

history.rationale: Cys47 completes the RING zinc coordination sphere; Tyr substitution abolishes ligase activity, though slightly lower confidence due to potential local structural tolerance.
C47 is a RING zinc ligand but structurally overlapping with C39/C44; retaining all four such candidates adds no diversity over the top two.

rejection.reason: C47 is a RING zinc ligand but structurally overlapping with C39/C44; retaining all four such candidates adds no diversity over the top two.
